decision.summary: Two regions warrant closer inspection: (1) a sharp multi-axis offset around index 440 with partial recovery in U but not E, and (2) a tightly bounded, coordinated triangular kink in all axes at the very end (725–729). Other sections show typical noise or smooth trends without ambiguous superposed changes.

regions.observation: Sharp ~12 MAD downward step in E and U components centered near index 440, with E dropping from ~-5 to ~-15 and U from ~0 to ~-10; N shows no corresponding step but exhibits increased noise. A possible partial return begins around 445 in U, but E remains offset—suggesting a temporary offset or incomplete recovery.

Linear trend reversal in all three components between indices 725–729: N drops sharply (~0.6 MAD), E rises (~1.4 MAD), and U falls (~1.6 MAD) over just 5 samples, forming a tight triangular kink. The abruptness and coordinated multi-axis change suggest a possible instrumental artifact or very rapid motion; the surrounding region (720–729) shows otherwise smooth behavior, highlighting this as anomalous.
